title: The Picture He Built Alone
description:
Three nights. A registry record, a line from an article a dozen years old, one remembered scene at a time.

The name he steered away from — Han PD Construction. The 'Lim' who vouched for Park Sang-jin to his father. The man who came up from a Chungcheong fishing town and reached Gangnam by stepping on people.

Three threads met at one point. Lim Sang-chul.

No one told him. Minjun built the man out of fragments.
And once he knew, the same seat in the same café looked different.

choices.text: Hold the cards — knowing is its own power
choices.result_text:
Minjun closed the notebook.

He wouldn't tear the man down, wouldn't forgive him either. He would simply know.
He'd sit at the same table knowing exactly who this man was.

This time, the one holding the cards was Minjun.

choices.text: See the man again — one day I'll ask him directly
choices.result_text:
Minjun looked at the Gangnam lights for a long time.

He wanted to ask. Why did you do it. Knowing, why did you let me in.

Not yet. But the question was inside him now, clear and waiting.

choices.text: Swallow it — Gangnam comes first for now
choices.result_text:
He wouldn't let on that he knew. He'd set the next meeting like nothing happened.

Someday this weight would come back around.
Until then — Gangnam first.

Minjun turned off the light. Sleep didn't come.

title: A Name That Stayed
description:
There was a name Sang-chul had quietly steered away from at the network dinner. "Han PD Construction."
Minjun filed it away in the back of his mind. Weeks passed.

Tonight, he couldn't sleep. He searched the name.
An old article. A real estate guarantee scam. A broker who made the introductions. The name was redacted — but the timing, the district, the pattern — it all mirrored what happened to his father.

And at the bottom of the article, in the list of related entities: Han PD Construction.
The same name Sang-chul's face hadn't changed at all while he deflected.

choices.text: Dig deeper — trace Sang-chul's old transactions
choices.result_text:
Registry records. Old articles. Corporate histories. He dug through all of it until dawn.

The pieces aligned. Same window. Same neighborhood. Same referral structure.

Lim. Sang. Chul.

Minjun's father never spoke the name. Minjun had found it himself.
The man who'd been teaching him to read charts — the same man who five years ago walked his father into financial ruin.

No one told him. He figured it out alone.
That weight was heavier.

choices.text: Leave it alone — he can't be sure
choices.result_text:
You can't accuse someone based on one article.
Minjun closed his laptop.

But — a suspicion, once caught, doesn't let go easily.
Every time he saw Sang-chul now, that name rang somewhere quiet inside him.

He'd pretend not to know. For now.

title: Father's Secret
description:
After the hospital visit, Dad started calling more often.
Short calls. How's the weather. Have you eaten.

Today was different.
He spoke slowly.
"Minjun. About that debt. It was... Park Sang-jin."

Minjun had never heard that name before.

"Someone from the Gangnam real estate scene introduced us. A man named Lim. He seemed decent at first... He said Park Sang-jin was someone you could trust."

Minjun set down the cup he'd been holding.

description_if_known.deduced_sangchul_truth:
After the hospital visit, Dad started calling more.
Short calls. Weather. Have you eaten.

Today was different.
He spoke slowly.
"Minjun. That debt. It was Park Sang-jin. A man named Lim introduced us."

Minjun already knew.
He'd pieced it together alone — in the small hours, from old articles and registry records.
Lim Sang-chul.

Hearing it from his father's mouth was different.
The weight he'd been carrying alone — now it belonged to both of them.

Minjun set his cup down slowly.
description_if_known.sangchul_clue_noted:
After the hospital visit, Dad started calling more.

Today was different.
He spoke slowly.
"Minjun. That debt. A man named Lim from the Gangnam real estate scene introduced us."

Minjun remembered.
The name that had passed through that dinner. The one he'd filed away and chosen not to dig into.
Not sure enough. Not yet.

Now he was sure.
The night he'd decided to leave it alone — suddenly felt very heavy.

choices.text: "That man named Lim — do you happen to know his full name?"
choices.result_text:
"Lim... Sang-chul, I think he said. Why?"

Minjun couldn't answer.

Lim. Sang. Chul.

The broker who ruined his father five years ago. That man is Minjun's mentor right now. The one who sits across from him at the same café, teaching him how to read charts.

The hand holding the phone went cold.

choices.text: "Do you know where he is now?"
choices.result_text:
"No idea. Somewhere in Gangnam, I suppose."

Minjun knows.

Not just somewhere in Gangnam — Lim Sang-chul still sits at the same table in the same café. Teaching Minjun how to trade charts.

Dad doesn't know. He has no idea that man has walked right into the middle of his son's life.

choices.text: (He couldn't say a word)
choices.result_text:
After a long silence, Dad spoke again.
"I just... felt like I had to tell you. I'm sorry, son."

Minjun couldn't even say "it's okay." He ended the call.
And sat alone in his room.

Lim Sang-chul.

title: Mirror
description:
Late at night, Sang-chul spoke.

"Minjun, can I be honest with you?"

{name} set down his glass.

"At first I just thought you were someone with drive.
But the more I watch you — you're like me.
You know how to move fast.
You know what you have to let go of."

{name} said nothing.

"I don't mean that as an insult. It's a compliment."

Through the window, Gangnam glittered.

choices.text: Raised his glass
choices.result_text:
They clinked glasses.
Sang-chul smiled.
{name} spent the whole walk home trying to figure out whether that was a compliment.

choices.text: "Do I seem that way?"
choices.result_text:
Sang-chul looked at him for a moment.
"You don't know? Or you're asking even though you do?"

{name} didn't answer.
Looked out the window.

choices.text: (He wanted to deny it)
choices.result_text:
"I'm a bit different."
Sang-chul nodded.
"If that's what you think, then sure."

{name} spent all night turning that over in his head.

title: The Question
description:
For a month, Minjun did nothing.
He still met Sang-chul. Talked like usual. Charts, markets, strategy for next month.

Then today, he reached his limit.

He set his coffee down and spoke.
"Sang-chul. Do you know a man named Park Sang-jin?"

choices.text: Waited for Sang-chul's reaction
choices.result_text:
Sang-chul's hand stopped.

He didn't deny it. He didn't pretend to be surprised.
He just — went quiet for a moment.

"...How did you find out?"
choices.foreshadow: He'd called it a partnership. The thought that he might someday call it something else flickered briefly, then passed.

choices.text: "Forget it." (He took it back)
choices.result_text:
Something shifted in Sang-chul's eyes.

He probably already knew what Minjun knew.

Minjun finished his coffee and stood up first. He still needs what this man knows. That's all this is.

Sang-chul said nothing.

choices.text: (He got up and left)
choices.result_text:
Minjun stood and walked out of the café without a word.

Sang-chul called his name from behind. He didn't turn around.

That relationship ended that day. With no dramatic scene.

description_if_known.used_sangchul_knowingly:
For a month, Minjun did nothing.
He still met Sang-chul. Talked like usual. Charts, markets, strategy for next month.
He took the deals Sang-chul handed him too. Knowing, and still taking them.

Then today, he reached his limit.

He set his coffee down and spoke.
"Sang-chul. Do you know a man named Park Sang-jin?"

He thought of the account he'd grown with that man's money.
Whether he had any right to ask this question — he didn't know.
description_if_known.sangchul_helped_with_father:
For a month, Minjun did nothing.
He still met Sang-chul. Talked like usual. Charts, markets, strategy for next month.

Then today, he reached his limit.

He set his coffee down and spoke.
"Sang-chul. Do you know a man named Park Sang-jin?"

The day Sang-chul handled his father's hospital situation came back to him.
Had that been the moment — when this man became his person.

title: I'm Sorry
description:
After a long silence, Sang-chul spoke.

"I knew he was your father. From the beginning."

Minjun didn't respond.

"When Park Sang-jin called and made the introduction... I just did him a favor. I didn't know it would go this far."

A beat of silence.

Sang-chul said,
"I'm sorry."

choices.text: "I'm going to report you."
choices.result_text:
Sang-chul nodded quietly.
"Yeah. That's the right call."

Minjun stood up. The network was gone. Everything Sang-chul knew was out of reach. Gangnam felt farther away.

And yet — for the first time, he could picture his father's face clearly.

choices.text: "That's all I needed to hear." (He let it go)
choices.result_text:
Sang-chul lifted his head and looked at Minjun.
"Thank you."

The words felt off. Thanking someone who was apologizing.

But maybe — maybe this is the right way. Not tearing everything apart and scrubbing it clean. Just letting it be.

choices.text: "I'm only here because of you." (He chose to use it)
choices.result_text:
Sang-chul paused.
"...You're going to use this."

Minjun smiled. It came out wrong.

This man destroyed his father. But without this man's network, Gangnam was impossible. So — this guilt was an asset too.

It was Jae-hyuk's move. Now Minjun was making it.

description_if_known.rationalized_using_people:
After a long silence, Sang-chul spoke.

"He's that man's son. I knew from the start."

Minjun said nothing.

"When Park Sang-jin reached out and asked me to look out for you... I just did what he asked. I didn't know it would become this."

Sang-chul said, "I'm sorry."

Minjun remembered something he'd once told himself.
'Everyone lives like this.'
It felt like Sang-chul was saying the exact same thing now.
Somewhere along the way, he too must have talked himself into it.
description_if_known.sangchul_called_you_his_mirror:
After a long silence, Sang-chul spoke.

"He's that man's son. I knew from the start."

{name} said nothing.

"When Park Sang-jin reached out and asked me to look out for you... I just did what he asked. I didn't know it would become this."

A silence between them.

Sang-chul said, "I'm sorry."

What he'd said once before — 'you're like me' — came back.
How those words sounded now was different.
description_if_known.denied_sangchul_mirror:
After a long silence, Sang-chul spoke.

"He's that man's son. I knew from the start."

{name} said nothing.

"When Park Sang-jin reached out and asked me to look out for you... I just did what he asked. I didn't know it would become this."

A silence between them.

Sang-chul said, "I'm sorry."

He remembered the night he'd said 'I'm a bit different.'
And Sang-chul nodding: 'if that's what you think, then sure.'
Sitting here now, those words had weight.

title: The Same Question
description:
A message from Jae-hyuk.

It had been a while. Contact had been sparse since the scam arc.

"Minjun. I've got an investment deal going — can you co-sign for me? Just this once."

Minjun set his phone down and stared out the window.

A guarantor.

That's what ruined his father.

choices.text: "No." (He refused, flat)
choices.result_text:
A pause.
Jae-hyuk replied: "Okay." That was it.

Minjun set his phone on the table and thought about his father.
His father must have had a moment like this. The moment he couldn't say no.

Minjun said no today. He still doesn't know if it was right. He just did it.

choices.text: "How much are we talking?" (He decided to hear it out)
choices.result_text:
Jae-hyuk explained. As Minjun listened, something felt off.

Was this guy hiding something again? Or — was this actually a solid deal this time?

Minjun signed the guarantee.

That's probably what his father thought too. "This time it'll be fine."
choices.foreshadow: Maybe his approach wasn't wrong. Gangnam needs people like this, he told himself.

choices.text: (He closed the message and pretended not to have seen it)
choices.result_text:
Minjun closed the message and opened another app.

Practical choice. He didn't want to be tangled up with Jae-hyuk anymore.

But on the day his father agreed to be a guarantor, that man probably reached out exactly like this.

Minjun put his phone in the drawer.

title: Three Times Absent
description:
The hospital called.

They said Dad was in critical condition. He needed to come down right away.

This wasn't the first time Minjun had gotten this call.

Three times. He hadn't gone down any of them. Something important came up. A deal. No time.

This call — was the fourth.

description_if_known.father_mentally_updated:
The hospital called.

They said Dad was in critical condition. He needed to come down right away.

Three times. He hadn't gone down any of them.

But there had been one real conversation.
{name} had told him — what he was doing, why he was in Seoul, how he was living.
Dad listened, quiet. Said he hoped things would work out.

That was the last thing he heard his father say.

choices.text: (He took the KTX. Knowing he was already too late.)
choices.result_text:
When he arrived at Changwon Station, Dad was already gone.

The nurse said "about an hour ago."

Minjun sat down beside the hospital bed. He stayed for a long time. There was nothing left.

He'd come to Seoul to show his father something.
That reason had left first.

choices.text: (He hung up. There was a deal he had to close right now.)
choices.result_text:
He made five million won on that deal.

The next morning, the call came again. Dad had passed away the night before.

Minjun set down his phone and looked at his bank balance.

The number had gone up.

title: Why Gangnam
description:
Late night. A milestone number finally crossed.

{name} sat looking at the screen for a while after the notification.

Somewhere in the middle of it all, the question surfaced:
"Why was it Gangnam in the first place?"

Back at the start — what was it that made that the destination?

choices.text: "To prove something."
choices.result_text:
To whom — {name} wasn't sure anymore.
To the people who wrote him off. To the hometown. Maybe to himself.

Somewhere along the way, the thing to prove had blurred.
But the legs had kept walking anyway.

choices.text: "I think I wanted to pay back my father's debt — my way."
choices.result_text:
Not the money. Not literally.

The debt of not being able to do anything then.
The debt of watching him collapse and just standing there.

{name} looked at the screen for a long time.
This was the real answer. It had been there the whole time.

choices.text: "I thought Gangnam would make things different. Now I'm not sure."
choices.result_text:
Different from what? Honestly — didn't know anymore.

The number on screen meant something. Just not exactly what {name} had imagined it would mean.

Maybe the answer comes when the destination is actually reached.
